title: August sales number for the stand-up
ticketBrief:
# Message from Priya, Sales Operations
> For Monday's stand-up I need the headline August number. Leadership only counts orders that were **delivered** — cancelled and returned orders don't count.

**Deliverable:** one row with `delivered_orders` (count) and `revenue` (sum of `amount`, rounded to 2 decimals) for orders placed in August 2026.

steps.title: Write the query
steps.instruction: Query the warehouse and return the single row requested.

config.groundTruthQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' AND order_date BETWEEN '2026-08-01' AND '2026-08-31'

public.prompt: Delivered orders and revenue for August 2026

hints.body: Filter on status first, then on the date range.

title: Delivered revenue by category
ticketBrief:
# Message from Priya, Sales Operations
> The category heads want to see how their categories did. Same rule as always: **delivered orders only**.

**Deliverable:** one row per product `category` with `orders` (count) and `revenue` (sum of `amount`, 2 decimals), highest revenue first.

steps.title: Write the query
steps.instruction: Join orders to products and aggregate by category.

config.groundTruthQuery: SELECT p.category, COUNT(*) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(o.amount), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.product_id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC

queries.by_cat: SELECT p.category, COUNT(*) c, ROUND(SUM(o.amount),2) r FROM orders o JOIN products p USING(product_id) WHERE o.status='delivered' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY r DESC

title: City-wise revenue (the city column is messy)
ticketBrief:
# Message from Arjun, Analytics Lead
> Regional managers get different numbers for the same city because the CRM stores `Mumbai` and `mumbai ` (and ` Delhi`) as different values. Clean it **in the query** — don't touch the table.

**Deliverable:** one row per cleaned city with `city` (trimmed, lower-case) and `revenue` (delivered orders only, 2 decimals), highest first.

steps.title: Write the query
steps.instruction: Normalise the city text and aggregate delivered revenue.

config.groundTruthQuery: SELECT LOWER(TRIM(c.city)) AS city, ROUND(SUM(o.amount), 2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY LOWER(TRIM(c.city)) ORDER BY revenue DESC

provenance.source: Synthetic dataset written by Capabilio for this challenge
provenance.license: Original content (no real people or businesses)

queries.by_city: SELECT lower(trim(c.city)) AS city, ROUND(SUM(o.amount),2) AS rev FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id WHERE o.status='delivered' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
